author: IGN
description:
In today's Daily Fix:
Sony has decided to delay God of War Laufey a few months to May 2027. Originally slated for February 2027, developer Sony Santa Monica said the game needs extra time to "make an extraordinary experience worth of the passion and dedication of our fans." This does free up a little room in a crowded post-holiday release calendar, with Fable, Metro 2039, and others still scheduled to be released around that time. In other news, Bloodborne still doesn't have a next-gen update, but Sony might not need one if the original keeps selling the way it is. According to industry analysts, Bloodborne sold 250,000 copies in 2026 alone, impressive for an 11-year-old game. And we’re heading back to How to Train Your Dragon’s Isle of Berk with the Ride Guys to soar through Hiccup’s Wing Gliders – all at Universal Orlando Resort.
Presented by Universal Orlando Resort, and its newest theme park, Universal Epic Universe.
title: God of War Laufey Pushed to May 2027 - IGN Daily Fix

description:
Will Elder Scrolls 6 Have Ship Combat and Mechs?
The worst-kept secret in RPGs is finally out in the open: The Elder Scrolls VI has officially received a title, Sentinel, and we’re heading straight into the sun-scorched, politically fraught province of Hammerfell. But behind the domed palaces and sand dunes lies a tangled nest of deep lore that hints at something far wilder than standard sword-and-sorcery. The prospect of open-ocean seafaring and god-powered, colossal Dwarven mechs. TES 6 hints at addressing the lingering fallout of Daggerfall’s "Warp in the West" and the scattered pieces of the Numidium, or Brass God. And, with an inevitable score to settle with the Aldmeri Dominion, we think Bethesda’s return to the Iliac Bay could deliver the studio’s most chaotic, kaiju-sized fantasy epic yet. 

Numidium, Hammerfell & The Fall of the Thalmor
In this lore breakdown for The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel, we examine the official Bethesda teaser, the cryptic prophecy from Moth Priest Yaz
title: Will Elder Scrolls 6 Have Ship Combat and Mechs?

author: IGN
description:
It’s time! The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is here, and it is amazing! Join Logan Plant, Peer Schneider, and Nick Limon as Logan breaks down his review of the highly-anticipated Switch 2 remake. From its gorgeous world stuffed with secrets to its wonderful modern controls reminiscent of more recent Zelda games, the panel discusses how it deepens an adventure that means so much to many people. And, they dive into why this is the perfect way for newer Zelda fans to jump into the traditional 3D Zelda formula that longtime fans adore. Hyrule awaits!

Presented by Best Buy Gamers.

#ocarinaoftime #nintendo #legendofzelda
title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Review Discussion - NVC 833

author: IGN
description:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time reviewed by Logan Plant on Nintendo Switch 2.

"It’s in our nature to pass old stories down, and I think there’s meaning in the ones we choose to revisit. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is both an exceptional remake of an incredible game and a rich adventure that stands on its own. This remake proves there’s still so much value in the traditional Zelda formula: the dense, intimate world of Hyrule is stuffed with charming characters and fascinating secrets. Its intricate dungeons are satisfying to unravel, even if their somewhat streamlined design has slightly dulled the special feeling that comes from solving them. Still, the depth, quality, and attention to detail in every corner match the lofty reputation of this series. Whether you’ve played the original 100 times, once back in 1998, or never at all, I highly recommend this beautiful retelling of a legend."

#IGN #Gaming #Nintendo
title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Review
